newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 30.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Peter Brock announced he would retire from motor racing at the end of this season, after 30 years in the sport. Brock's career is unparalleled, winning both Bathurst and Sandown nine times, and the national touring car championship three times. Page 21.

The Women's National Basketball League has called a council meeting to reconsider its move to a summer competition next year, with clubs seeking to discuss the change in more detail. There is also concern that Australia's best players might leave the WNBL to play overseas during a summer season. Page 20.

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor's poor form continued yesterday, when he was dismissed lbw for 30 in Australia's second innings against Gloucestershire. Taylor made a duck in the first innings, putting further pressure on the tour selectors deciding his future. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Representatives of the Australian Jockey Club and the Sydney Turf Club met last night to discuss a reconciliation over night racing and training facilities. A decision will be made within two weeks on whether night racing will be held in Canterbury or Randwick. A working party has been set up to address the problem of training facilities, where currently the AJC carries most of the financial load. Page 47.

Parramatta coach Brian Smith and North Sydney coach Peter Louis yesterday attacked the Australian Rugby League for scheduling tonight's match so close to Wednesday's State of Origin. Both clubs have five players going into tonight's match who also played in the Origin game. The ARL defended the schedule, saying the draw was made before the representative teams were picked. Page 47.

Carlton player Greg Williams' manager Peter Jess said the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Williams' nine-week suspension, handed down by the Australian Football League for interfering with an umpire, could have a serious effect on how sport is administered in Australia. Jess said the decision acknowledged that players' livelihoods were at stake with each Tribunal hearing, and that the decision gave the players the same rights as people in the corporate world. Page 47.
THE AGE

The Victorian Racing Club announced a revamp of the four-day Melbourne Cup festival. There will be 10 races on Melbourne Cup day with the extra race run early to cater for people arriving at the track early. The VRC also announced nine races on Derby Day, widely acknowledged as Australia's greatest race day. Page D13.

Sprinter Dean Capobianco will seek to have his four-year suspension for a positive steroid test overturned, when the International Amateur Athletics Federation meets in Athens this weekend. The IAAF Council will hear a lengthy submission for the sprinter' reinstatement. Page D12.

Melbourne captain Garry Lyon will play against Richmond in its Australian Football League game tomorrow night, just days after conceding his season might be over. Lyon has missed the past five weeks with a chronic back injury, but volunteered himself for tomorrow's match. Lyon said he may need surgery on his back later in the season, but said there was no major risk he could do further damage. Page D2.
THE HERALD SUN

Super League chief John Ribot has forecast crowds of 15,000 and a A$10 million turnover in the first year of Melbourne's Super League team, which is to feature high-profile Australian representatives. However, Ribot said Super League would not invest money in the proposed home ground, Docklands Stadium. Page 90.

Melbourne president Joseph Gutnick promised greater support for the Australian Football League club's next coach after the sacking of their coach of five years Neil Balme yesterday. Gutnick said he did not believe Balme was the right coach for the type ofteam Melbourne has at the moment. Page 104.

Brisbane racing analyst Dave Parker has used a computer to find that jockey Shane Dye has a major-race strike rate unprecedented in modern times. Of his last 60 major races, Dye has won 20 and recorded a place in a further 20. Page 92.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Millionaire racehorse owner Helen Dalton sought to take possession of an unraced two year old from Gai Waterhouse's stables at Randwick yesterday, but was refused permission because Waterhouse's father Tommy Smith holds shares in the horse. Dalton wanted to give the horse to a different trainer due to a disagreement with Smith. Page 128.

Balmain and international rugby league fullback Tim Brasher has been granted permission to negotiate with other Australian Rugby League and Super League clubs, after Brasher declined an offer from Balmain earlier this year. Brasher is now able to find outthe value of his contract. Page 123.

The Australian Rugby League has voted out long-term Australian team manager Geoff Carr at a board meeting in Brisbane this week. Former test winger Kerry Boustead has filled the position and will manage the Australian team for its game against the Rest ofthe World on June 11. Page 123.
